title: A person's wording in a translation is never overwritten by a machine
description:
As an editor, I want blocks of a translation that a person edited to be pinned, so the next machine re-translation keeps them and shows me a conflict when the original changed underneath them.

Design: alignment JSON in S3 beside each localization version (target block -> source block hash, owner machine|human, pinned). Saving a person's edit pins the changed blocks; a source change re-translates only changed machine blocks; a pinned block whose source changed becomes a conflict; the localization is marked diverged while pinned blocks exist. Depends on the alignment spike. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450).

Feature: Pinned human wording

Scenario: A local readability edit survives re-translation
  Given a Spanish paragraph a person reworded
  And the English paragraph it came from is unchanged
  When a later English edit to another paragraph is translated
  Then the reworded Spanish paragraph is kept exactly
  And only the Spanish paragraph for the edited English paragraph changes

Scenario: The original changes under a person's wording
  Given a Spanish paragraph a person reworded
  When the English paragraph it came from is rewritten
  Then the Spanish paragraph is not overwritten
  And the localization shows a conflict with the old original, the new original, the person's wording and a new machine proposal
  And it cannot be published until an editor resolves the conflict
